title: Time 2: в понедельник (on a day, at a time)
titleRussian: Время 2: в понедельник (в какой день, в котором часу)
description: To say something happens ON a day or AT a clock time, use в + accusative: в понедельник (on Monday), в среду (on Wednesday), в два часа (at two o'clock). For most days the accusative looks like the dictionary form; feminine -а days change to -у (среда → среду).
descriptionRussian: Чтобы сказать, что что-то происходит В какой-то день или В котором часу, используют в + винительный падеж: в понедельник, в среду, в два часа. У большинства дней винительный совпадает со словарной формой; дни на -а женского рода меняют его на -у (среда → среду).
intro: One preposition covers two different jobs: saying which day something happens and saying at what time. Both take the accusative, so learning one gets you the other. Most days do not change shape at all; only the feminine ones do. And one day takes a slightly longer form of the preposition, purely to make it easier to say.
rules: To say something happens ON a day, use в + accusative: в понедельник, в четверг, в воскресенье.
Most days look the same in the accusative as in the dictionary form, so you just add в (or во before вторник): в понедельник, во вторник, в четверг.
Feminine days ending in -а change -а to -у in the accusative: среда → в среду, пятница → в пятницу, суббота → в субботу.
The same в + accusative says AT a clock time: в два часа, в пять часов, в час. The number keeps the час/часа/часов form from Lesson 1.
Use во (not в) before вторник to smooth the consonant cluster: во вторник.
examples: Я работаю в понедельник. (I work on Monday.) понедельник = accusative = dictionary form.
Во вторник у меня урок. (On Tuesday I have a lesson.) во before вторник.
В среду мы отдыхаем. (On Wednesday we rest.) среда → среду, feminine -а → -у.
В пятницу будет концерт. (On Friday there will be a concert.) пятница → пятницу.
Магазин открывается в девять часов. (The shop opens at nine o'clock.) в + accusative for the clock time.
Встреча в два часа. (The meeting is at two o'clock.) в два часа, the Lesson 1 hour form returns.

tables.title: Days of the week: dictionary form → в + accusative

items.hint: Среда is feminine and ends in -а. What happens to -а in the accusative?
items.explanation: After в for a day we use the accusative. Feminine nouns in -а change -а to -у: среда → среду. So 'on Wednesday' is в среду.

items.promptEnglish: On Monday I have a Russian lesson.
items.hint: Понедельник is masculine. Its accusative looks just like the dictionary form.
items.explanation: Masculine inanimate days do not change in the accusative, so you simply add в: в понедельник. The preposition в is required to mean 'on (a day).'

items.promptEnglish: The concert will be on Friday.
items.explanation: Пятница ends in -а, so its accusative is пятницу. 'On Friday' = в пятницу. The pattern matches в среду and в субботу.

items.hint: Before the cluster в + вт, Russian adds a vowel to the preposition.
items.explanation: Before вторник the preposition becomes во to ease the consonant cluster: во вторник. The case is still accusative; only the spelling of the preposition changes.

items.promptEnglish: The shop closes at ten o'clock.
items.hint: в + accusative for the clock time; the number is 10, so the Lesson 1 rule applies.
items.explanation: For a clock time we use в + accusative: в десять часов. The hour form follows Lesson 1: 10 is in the '5 and up' group, so часов.

items.promptEnglish: The lesson starts at two o'clock.
items.hint: 'At two o'clock' uses the plain counting number plus часа.
items.explanation: 'At two o'clock' is в два часа: the number два sits in the accusative phrase and часа follows the 2-4 rule. (We say два, not две, with the masculine noun час.)

blanks: Мы встречаемся в _____. (We are meeting on Saturday.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Суббота is feminine in -а, so the accusative after в is субботу: в субботу.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each day by what its в-form does: stays the same, or changes -а to -у.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The concert will be on Saturday.
errorCorrection.explanation: After в for a day the noun is accusative, and a feminine -а noun changes -а to -у: суббота becomes субботу. So 'on Saturday' is в субботу.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The concert will be on Friday.
errorCorrection.explanation: To pin an event to a single day, Russian uses в + accusative, not на: в пятницу ('on Friday'). На is the wrong preposition for a weekday here (it shows up in other time phrases like на этой неделе, but not with single days). The accusative пятницу is already correct; only the preposition needs to change to в.

For 'on a day' Russian uses в + accusative, so суббота becomes субботу: в субботу. The form субботе is the prepositional, which English speakers reach for because в often means 'in a place' with the prepositional, but for a day in time it is the accusative. The correct phrase is в субботу.

minimalPairs.explanation: After в for a day the noun is accusative. Среда is feminine -а, so it becomes среду. The dictionary form среда (nominative) cannot follow в here.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: On Tuesday I have a meeting.
minimalPairs.explanation: Before вторник the preposition takes the extra vowel: во вторник. Plain в would be hard to pronounce against the в + вт cluster, so во is the correct form.

reviewVocab.definition: the construction for 'on a day' and 'at a clock time': в понедельник, в среду, в два часа, в пять часов.
reviewVocab.example: В пятницу в семь часов у нас концерт.

reviewVocab.definition: the accusative of the three feminine -а days; the -а changes to -у after в.
'on Tuesday'; the preposition becomes во (not в) to ease the cluster before вторник.
